GOOGL.rationale: GOOGL's fundamental health is strong — revenue accelerating +24.2% YoY to $119.8B, operating margins expanding to 34%, Cloud revenue surging 82% to $24.8B with $514B backlog, and a fortress balance sheet with $242.5B cash. However, the valuation signal is deeply distorted and the stock is unattractive on a normalized basis. The headline PE of 19x is at the floor of its 365-day range (18.1-39.5x), but this is entirely an artifact of a $94B unrealized gain on SpaceX that inflated Q2 net income to $112.19B — 2.75x operating income of $40.77B. On sustainable operating earnings (~$2.80-3.50 EPS run-rate), the normalized PE is ~95-120x, far above the stock's historical 25-39x range. The market has partially recognized this: the stock declined ~6-7% post-earnings despite the headline beat, and is 18% below its 251-bar high. Additionally, 2026 capex guidance was raised to $195-205B, creating negative free cash flow for the first time, and Gemini 3.5 Pro delays raise execution concerns. The antitrust structural remedy risk (potential Chrome/Android divestiture) adds further downside. The combination of illusory cheapness on distorted earnings, massive capex commitment pressuring FCF, AI model execution uncertainty, and regulatory overhang makes this strongly unattractive at current levels.
key_factors: Headline PE of 19x is misleadingly low — inflated by $94B unrealized SpaceX gain that made net income 2.75x operating income ($112.19B vs $40.77B); normalized PE on operating earnings is ~95-120x vs historical 25-39x range
